plan.notes: Source: official Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology Academic Catalog (2026-2027 edition), Computer Science (BS) page 'Plan of Study Grid' sample plan of study, 'New Curriculum Starting Fall 2026': https://catalog.rose-hulman.edu/catalog/undergraduate-programs-study/computer-science-bs/ Cross-checked against the catalog's official plan PDF: https://catalog.rose-hulman.edu/catalog/undergraduate-programs-study/computer-science-bs/computer-science-bs_planofstudytext.pdf. Transcription method: fetched the live catalog page and the linked official plan PDF on 2026-09-30; all course codes, titles, and credit hours copied verbatim from the official grid. Rose-Hulman runs on a quarter system, so this plan has 12 quarters (Fall/Winter/Spring x 4 years), not 8 semesters. Per-term printed totals (18+17+17+16+16+16+16+16+16+16+16+12) sum to the catalog's published degree total of 192 credits, which is used as total_credits. Caveats: (1) The sample plan is track-generic: six 4-credit slots are printed only as 'Track Required Course' with no course assigned, so they are transcribed as choice slots listing the official track course codes; see each slot's choice_note. CS majors choose the Developer track (Software Development, Industry, & Practice) or the Researcher track (Theory, Applications, & Research). (2) Elective split discrepancy: the printed plan contains eight HSSA elective slots (32 cr) and four free-elective slots (16 cr), while the catalog's prose requirements state 28 HSS credits and 20 free-elective credits; both sum to 48 elective credits and the plan total still matches the published 192. (3) The official sample plan lists no prerequisites, so all prereq fields are empty; students must consult the catalog course descriptions and their advisor for prerequisite chains. (4) PH 111L/PH 112L are 0-credit required labs, flagged required_zero. (5) Older track flowchart PDFs linked from the page (Jan/Jul 2025) predate the Fall 2026 curriculum and were not used for term placement.

courses.title: Track Required Course
courses.choice_note: The official sample plan lists this as a generic 4-credit 'Track Required Course' slot and does not assign a specific course to it. Developer track requires CSSE 371, CSSE 374, CSSE 376, CSSE 477, and CSSE 497-499 (CSSE 371 and the senior capstone sequence appear as named slots elsewhere in this plan). Researcher track requires CSSE 193, CSSE 392, CSSE 393, CSSE 394, CSSE 395, and CSSE 474 or MA 474, plus MA 371 and either CSSE 487-489 or CSSE 494-496 (MA 371 and the senior project sequence appear as named slots elsewhere). Remaining track slots are filled with 300-level-or-above CSSE electives (or ECE 332) toward the 16-credit additional-CSSE requirement. See academic advisor.

courses.title: CSSE Elective, 300-level or above (student choice)
courses.choice_note: Student choice: 4 credits of additional 300-level or above CSSE courses (or ECE 332); excludes CSSE 490-493, CSSE 487-489, and CSSE 494-496; advisor approval required.
